# migrator

```go
import "github.com/brpaz/lib-go/db/migrator"
```

Package migrator runs database schema migrations using goose.

### Basic usage

Pass an \*sql.DB and an fs.FS containing SQL files under a "migrations/" sub\-path. Callers typically embed the files and pass the resulting embed.FS:

```
//go:embed migrations/*.sql
var migrationsFS embed.FS

m, err := migrator.NewMigrator(db, migrationsFS)
```

[Migrator.Migrate](<#Migrator.Migrate>) applies all pending UP migrations. [Migrator.Rollback](<#Migrator.Rollback>) reverts the last applied migration. [Migrator.Status](<#Migrator.Status>) logs the current applied/pending state.

### Logging

By default the migrator discards all output. Supply a [Logger](<#Logger>) via [WithLogger](<#WithLogger>) to route migration output to your preferred sink:

```
m, err := migrator.NewMigrator(db, fsys,
    migrator.WithLogger(migrator.NewLibLogger(appLogger)),
)
```

[NewLibLogger](<#NewLibLogger>) wraps a [github.com/brpaz/lib\\\-go/logging.Logger](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/brpaz/lib-go/logging/#Logger>). [NewNopLogger](<#NewNopLogger>) discards output. Any value that implements [Logger](<#Logger>) \(Printf \+ Fatalf\) is accepted, so adapters for zap, logrus, or other libraries can be plugged in directly.

### Concurrency

goose uses package\-level global state \(base FS, dialect, table name\). Avoid running multiple Migrator instances concurrently with different options.

<a name="Logger"></a>
## type Logger

Logger is the logging interface consumed by [Migrator](<#Migrator>). It mirrors the goose.Logger contract so any adapter that satisfies goose also satisfies this interface.

```go
type Logger interface {
    Printf(format string, v ...any)
    Fatalf(format string, v ...any)
}
```

<a name="NewLibLogger"></a>
### func NewLibLogger

```go
func NewLibLogger(l *logging.Logger) Logger
```

NewLibLogger returns a Logger backed by a \[logging.Logger\]. Printf maps to Info; Fatalf maps to Error followed by os.Exit\(1\).

<a name="NewNopLogger"></a>
### func NewNopLogger

```go
func NewNopLogger() Logger
```

NewNopLogger returns a Logger that discards all output.

<a name="Migrator"></a>
## type Migrator

Migrator runs database schema migrations using goose.

Note: goose uses package\-level global state \(base FS, dialect, table name\). Avoid running multiple Migrator instances concurrently with different options.

```go
type Migrator struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="NewMigrator"></a>
### func NewMigrator

```go
func NewMigrator(db *sql.DB, fsys fs.FS, opts ...Option) (*Migrator, error)
```

NewMigrator constructs a Migrator. fsys must contain the SQL migration files. By default migrations are read from the root of fsys; use [WithMigrationsDir](<#WithMigrationsDir>) to specify a sub\-directory \(e.g. when using //go:embed migrations/\*.sql from a parent package\).

<a name="Option"></a>
## type Option

Option is a functional option for configuring the Migrator.

```go
type Option func(*Migrator)
```

<a name="WithDialect"></a>
### func WithDialect

```go
func WithDialect(dialect string) Option
```

WithDialect sets the SQL dialect used by goose. Defaults to "postgres". Valid values are the dialect names accepted by goose.SetDialect.

<a name="WithLogger"></a>
### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(logger Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger used for migration output. Use [NewLibLogger](<#NewLibLogger>) or [NewNopLogger](<#NewNopLogger>), or supply any [Logger](<#Logger>) implementation.

<a name="WithMigrationsDir"></a>
### func WithMigrationsDir

```go
func WithMigrationsDir(dir string) Option
```

WithMigrationsDir sets the directory within fsys that contains the SQL files. Defaults to "." \(root of fsys\). Use this when the embed FS contains a named sub\-directory, e.g. WithMigrationsDir\("migrations"\).
